purpose: Diazepam is used to help with anxiety, panic, and nervousness. It can also help relax tight or spasming muscles, treat alcohol withdrawal symptoms, and stop or prevent certain types of seizures. Doctors sometimes use it before medical procedures to help you feel calm and relaxed.
how_it_works: Your brain has natural calming chemicals, and diazepam helps those chemicals work more effectively. Think of it like turning down the volume on an overactive nervous system. This helps reduce anxiety, relax muscles, and calm electrical activity in the brain that can cause seizures.
common_side_effects: Feeling sleepy or drowsy, dizziness, feeling unsteady or clumsy, blurred vision, tiredness or weakness, and memory problems. Some people also feel confused or have trouble concentrating. These effects are stronger when you first start taking it.
warnings: This medicine can be habit-forming, so it should only be taken exactly as prescribed and not shared with anyone else. Do NOT drink alcohol while taking diazepam — this can be very dangerous and even life-threatening. Do not drive or operate heavy machinery until you know how it affects you. Do not stop taking it suddenly without talking to your doctor, as this can cause serious withdrawal symptoms. Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, as it can harm the baby.
typical_dosing: For adults, the usual dose for anxiety is 2 mg to 10 mg taken 2 to 4 times a day, depending on your condition. Your doctor will start you on the lowest dose that works for you. Older adults usually start with a lower dose because they are more sensitive to its effects. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions.
